source_text: XVI. Πέρας γοῦν ἰδόντες οἱ ἄνομοι μὴ δυνάμενον αὐτοῦ τὸ σῶμα ὑπὸ τοῦ πυρὸς δαπανηθῆναι, ἐκέλευσαν προσελθόντα αὐτῷ κονφέκτορα παραβῦσαι ξιφίδιον. Καὶ τοῦτο ποιήσαντος ἐξῆλθε [περιστερὰ καὶ] πλῆθος αἵματος, ὥστε κατασβέσαι τὸ πῦρ καὶ θαυμάσαι πάντα τὸν ὄχλον, εἰ τοσαύτη τις διαφορὰ μεταξὺ τῶν τε ἀπίστων καὶ τῶν ἐκλεκτῶν· ὧν εἷς καὶ οὗτος γεγόνει ὁ θαυμασιώτατος [μάρτυς] Πολύκαρπος, ἐν τοῖς καθ᾽ ἡμᾶς χρόνοις διδάσκαλος ἀποστολικὸς καὶ προφητικὸς γενόμενος, ἐπίσκοπος τῆς ἐν Σμύρνῃ καθολικῆς ἐκκλησίας. Πᾶν γὰρ ῥῆμα, ὃ ἀφῆκεν ἐκ τοῦ στόματος αὐτοῦ, ἐτελειώθη καὶ τελειωθήσεται.
thought_title: Blood coming out quenches the fire
orientation: The Smyrnaean letter-writers narrate what the executioners did when the fire did not consume Polycarp's body.
pass_a_gloss: Well then, when the lawless men saw that his body was not able to be consumed by the fire, they ordered the confector, after he came up to him, to thrust through with a small dagger. And when he did this, there came out [a dove and] a multitude of blood, so that it quenched the fire and all the crowd wondered, that there is so great a difference between the unbelieving and the elect; of whom this most wonderful [martyr] Polycarp also became one, having become in the times with us an apostolic and prophetic teacher, bishop of the universal church in Smyrna. For every word which he let go out of his mouth was completed and will be completed.

choices.why: keeps moral-legal judgment of persecutors, distinct from crowd and proconsul
preserves Latin loan office for arena attendant who dispatches, not generic soldier

choices.english: to thrust through with a small dagger
choices.why: keeps stabbing force and diminutive weapon, not killing generally

choices.term: τῶν τε ἀπίστων καὶ τῶν ἐκλεκτῶν
choices.why: keeps paired contrast unbelief versus chosen status without importing godless-people insult
required fixed glossary sense of worldwide shared congregation

pass_b_english: When the lawless men saw that the fire could not consume his body, they ordered a confector to step up to him and thrust him through with a small dagger. When he did so, so much blood poured out that it quenched the fire, and the whole crowd marveled that so great a difference should stand between the unbelieving and the elect. One of the elect was this most wonderful martyr Polycarp, who in our own time became an apostolic and prophetic teacher and bishop of the universal church in Smyrna. For every word he uttered has been fulfilled and will be fulfilled.
notes: The source brackets περιστερὰ καὶ and μάρτυς as doubtful text; the gloss keeps them bracketed and claims nothing from them.
κονφέκτορα is a Latin loanword spelling; παραβῦσαι is an unusual form for a dagger thrust, glossed by its plain force here.
